title: Refactoring: code smells and what to do about them

videos.script: Every codebase has a file that everybody is afraid to touch. {{title}} It works, more or less. It is long, it repeats itself, and nobody remembers why half of it is there. Refactoring is how you change that file without breaking it. {{file}} Not a rewrite. A rewrite stops the program working for weeks. A refactoring is a series of small moves, and after each one the program still runs and still gives the same answers. {{moves}} In this lesson you take a legacy report from the library and improve it six times. {{report}} First you pin down what it does today, with a test that compares its output to a saved copy. {{net}} Then you follow the smells. A function that does everything. The same line written twice. Money held in a bare integer. {{smells}} Three fields that always travel together, and a switch on a type code that appears in two places. {{switch}} At the end the report prints exactly what it printed at the start. Every byte. What changed is how easy the next change will be. {{end}}
